To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rs1447295 risk variant is associated with aggressive PCa, and the rs6983267 variant is associated with PCa presence.
rs1447295 was associated with aggressive disease, and rs698326 was associated with PCa presence.
rs1447295 GG genotype is associated with aggressive disease and rs69832671 GG genotype is associated to PCa presence in a Caucasian population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new biomarkers of prostate cancer aggressiveness.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms of prostate cancer development and progression.
identifying the genes and genetic pathways that contribute to the risk, progression, and response to therapy of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genotyping is not ready for prime time in clinical practice.
genetic testing of the 8q24 and 17p12 SNPs is of no use in the clinical setting for the time being.
genotyping of SNPs in PCa patients is not yet ready for prime time in the clinical setting, but the potential value of this approach is being actively explored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rs1447295 is associated with aggressive PCa, and rs6983263 is associated with PCa risk.
genotyping of rs1447296 and rs6983266 could be used to help in clinical decision-making in men with PSA >4 ng/mL and/or abnormal DRE.
the rs6983267 variant was significantly associated with the presence and the rs1447295 variant with the aggressiveness of the PCa in our population.

the 8q24 SNP rs6983267 is significantly associated with the outcome of prostatic biopsies in Caucasian men.
the genetic background of patients may influence the outcome of a biopsy.
